Units the system makes a month

answer: A typical 5 marla house with fans, LED lights, an inverter fridge, a TV, one 1.5 ton inverter AC, a water pump and an iron needs a solar system of about {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW ({{out.panels|int}} panels of {{out.panel_w|int}} W) with an on-grid inverter of {{out.inverter_buy}}. The panels are sized from the daily units ÷ the city's sun yield; the grid covers the moments when everything runs at once.
how: Energy: each appliance's watts × quantity × hours a day (an inverter AC counts at its average draw, below its rated watts), added up = {{out.daily_kwh|1}} units a day; ÷ {{out.yield_kwh_per_kwp_day|1}} units per kW of panels a day for your city = {{out.kw_energy|2}} kW. A grid-tied or hybrid system is sized by energy: when the {{out.running_w|int}} W running load is more than the panels give at that moment, the grid supplies the rest. {{out.kw|2}} kW needs {{out.panels|int}} panels of {{out.panel_w}} W = {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW installed, which makes about {{out.monthly_kwh_estimate|int}} units a month. {{out.inverter_text}}
key_facts: A typical 5 marla house with one 1.5 ton inverter AC has a running load of about {{out.running_w|int}} W and uses about {{out.daily_kwh|1}} units a day, so it needs a solar system of about {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW with an inverter of {{out.inverter_buy}}.
Solar system size in kW = units a day ÷ sun yield per kW a day. With the grid connected the panels do not have to carry every appliance at once; only an off-grid system is sized that way.
One kW of panels makes about {{out.yield_kwh_per_kwp_day|1}} units a day in Lahore over the year, so a {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW system makes about {{out.monthly_kwh_estimate|int}} units a month.
Panels are counted up to the next whole panel: {{out.kw|2}} kW ÷ {{out.panel_w|int}} W = {{out.panels|int}} panels, about {{out.roof_m2|int}} square metres of roof.

formula.text: kW = E_day ÷ yield (grid-tied or hybrid; P_run ÷ 1000 ÷ PR is the off-grid rule, shown for comparison); panels = ceil(kW × 1000 ÷ W_panel)
lines: E_day = Σ (watts × qty × hours) ÷ 1000, units used a day
yield = units one kW of panels makes a day in your city
P_run = total running watts, PR = performance ratio

On-grid inverter W = kW × 1000 ÷ r_max, r_max = largest panel-to-inverter (DC/AC) ratio; hybrid (backup hours set): max(P_run × margin, kW × 1000 ÷ r_max), surge ≥ largest starting load; then the next size sold
Battery Ah = P_run × night hours ÷ (V × DoD × η)

sections.h2: What is the electrical load of a 5 marla house?
p: A 5 marla house usually has two or three bedrooms, a lounge, a kitchen and one or two bathrooms. The default list above is what runs in such a house in summer: four ceiling fans, ten LED bulbs, an inverter fridge, a TV, one 1.5 ton inverter AC, a water pump and an iron. Together they come to {{out.running_w|int}} W running and {{out.daily_kwh|1}} units a day, which is about {{out.monthly_kwh_estimate|int}} units a month from the solar system.

The daily units, not the running load, set the panel size here. The AC, the pump and the fans can all be on at noon, and when their {{out.running_w|int}} W is more than the panels give, the grid supplies the rest. The panels also set an on-grid inverter, which runs beside the grid; the running load sets a hybrid inverter, which carries the house in a power cut. If your house has fewer or more appliances, change the list and the result updates.

sections.h2: How many kW solar for a 5 marla house?
p: For the typical house above the answer is {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW of panels with an inverter of {{out.inverter_buy}}. The energy rule asks for {{out.kw_energy|2}} kW. Panels big enough to carry the whole {{out.running_w|int}} W at midday ({{out.running_w|int}} W ÷ {{out.pr|2}} = {{out.kw_power|2}} kW) would make more units than the house uses, and the extra would be sold at the low buyback rate; that rule is for off-grid systems, which have no grid to fall back on.

The panel count is rounded up, so the installed size is a little above the calculated {{out.kw|2}} kW. Installers quote by inverter size: with no battery this house takes an on-grid inverter of {{out.inverter_buy}}, and a five kW one leaves room for more panels later. With a battery for power cuts the hybrid inverter must carry the {{out.running_w|int}} W running load, so it needs at least {{out.inverter_kw_load|up2}} kW.

Do not put every panel in one string. On a cold morning each {{out.panel_w|int}} W panel gives about {{out.panel_voc_cold_v|int}} V open-circuit, so {{out.panels|int}} panels in series would be about {{out.array_voc_cold_v|int}} V; split them into strings that each stay below the inverter's maximum DC input voltage on its datasheet.

sections.h2: When is a 5 kW solar system right for a 5 marla house?
p: {{out.panels|int}} panels on an on-grid inverter of at least {{out.inverter_kw|up2}} kW suit a 5 marla house with one inverter AC, fans, lights, a fridge and a pump, which is exactly the default above, so a five kW on-grid system covers it. It runs the whole house in the day and feeds spare units to the grid.
With two inverter ACs the daily units rise, so the panels and the inverter move up a size, and a hybrid inverter must carry both ACs at once. See the second worked example below for that house.

sections.h2: Solar for a 5 marla house with one AC
p: One 1.5 ton inverter AC is the single biggest load in the list. On average it draws about {{d.ac_inverter_avg_kw_1_5_ton|1}} kW while running, which is most of the house's daily units in summer. The default result is the one-AC case: {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW of panels and an inverter of {{out.inverter_buy}}.

If the AC is non-inverter, its starting surge is much larger. An on-grid inverter does not have to start it, because the grid does; a hybrid inverter that runs the AC in a power cut must, so enter backup hours and the result shows the surge rating it needs.

sections.h2: What does a 5 marla solar system cost?
p: An on-grid system of this size ({{out.installed_kw|2}} kW of panels, no battery) costs about {{px.out.price_low_rs|rsm}} to {{px.out.price_high_rs|rsm}} ({{px.out.price_low_rs|lakh}} to {{px.out.price_high_rs|lakh}}) installed, from the installer price lists and reports checked on {{px.checked}}; a battery and a hybrid inverter add to that. Prices move with the dollar rate, so check today's range with the [[D14|solar system price calculator]], ask for quotes in Rs per watt of panels so they compare like for like, and test a quote you have with the [[N3|solar quote checker]]. Month-to-month changes are in [[solar-price-tracker|this month's solar prices]].

A complete quote must include the panels, the inverter, the mounting structure, DC and AC cables, breakers and surge protection, earthing, installation labour and, for a grid-tied system, the net billing application and the bidirectional meter. A quote that leaves any of these out looks cheaper than it is.
For other house sizes see the [[D12|10 marla solar system]] and the [[D13|1 kanal solar system]].

sections.h2: Do you need a battery for a 5 marla solar system?
p: A grid-tied system with no battery is the cheapest and runs the house in the day; at night you buy from the grid. If your area has load shedding after sunset, enter the hours of backup you want and the calculator adds a lithium battery sized for the full running load for those hours.

The battery figure is for every appliance in your list running after dark. Most houses run only fans, lights and the fridge at night, so make a second list without the AC and pump to size a smaller battery.

mistakes: Sizing the panels to run every appliance at once. That is the off-grid rule; with the grid connected it buys panels whose extra units are sold back at the low buyback rate.
Forgetting the pump and iron. They run for minutes, but they are on the running load when they do, and the pump's starting surge sets a hybrid inverter's surge rating.

Mixing up the two inverter rules. An on-grid inverter is sized from the panels, which may be up to {{d.dc_ac_ratio_max|1}} times its rating; a hybrid inverter also carries the house in a power cut, so it is sized from the running load with a margin. A hybrid inverter smaller than the running load trips when the AC and the pump run together.

Expecting the rated panel watts every day. The performance ratio of {{d.pr|pct}} covers heat, dust, cable loss and cloudy days; the units a month shown is the realistic yearly average, not a sunny-day peak.
Sizing a battery for the whole house. The battery line assumes every listed appliance runs after dark; list only the night loads for a battery you can afford.
safety: A rooftop solar system connects to the grid and to your house wiring at mains voltage; have a licensed electrician and a AEDB-certified installer do the wiring, earthing and net billing connection.

faq.q: How many solar panels does a 5 marla house need?
faq.a: The typical 5 marla house above needs {{out.panels|int}} panels of {{out.panel_w|int}} W, which is {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW and about {{out.roof_m2|int}} square metres of roof. Smaller panels mean more panels for the same kW.

faq.q: Is a 5 kW solar system enough for a 5 marla house?
faq.a: Yes for one 1.5 ton inverter AC with fans, lights, a fridge and a pump on the grid: the house needs {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW of panels and an on-grid inverter of at least {{out.inverter_kw|up2}} kW. A hybrid inverter with a battery also carries the house in a power cut, so it must be at least {{out.inverter_kw_load|up2}} kW for the whole list; put only the loads you need in a cut on the battery side to keep it smaller. For two ACs at the same time, or an electric geyser, the calculator moves to the next size.

faq.q: How many units will a 5 marla solar system make a month?
faq.a: About {{out.monthly_kwh_estimate|int}} units a month for the {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW system in Lahore, as a yearly average. Summer months make more and winter months less; choose your city above for its own sun yield.

faq.q: Can I run a 1.5 ton AC on a 5 marla solar system?
faq.a: Yes. The panels make the house's daily units, the AC's included, and when the AC and the rest together draw more than the panels give at that moment, the grid supplies the difference. In the evening the AC runs from the grid or from a battery.

faq.q: What is the price of a solar system for a 5 marla house?
faq.a: About {{px.out.price_low_rs|rsm}} to {{px.out.price_high_rs|rsm}} installed for a {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW on-grid system with no battery, from price lists checked on {{px.checked}}. Compare quotes in Rs per watt for the complete system, including structure, cables, protection, installation and the net billing application, and check one with the [[N3|solar quote checker]].

faq.q: Grid-tied, hybrid or off-grid for a 5 marla house?
faq.a: Grid-tied is cheapest and sells spare units to the grid. Hybrid adds a battery for load shedding, sized with the backup hours field above. Off-grid needs a battery for every night and cloudy day and is rarely worth it where the grid is available.

faq.q: Why does the result change when I add an appliance that runs for a few minutes?
faq.a: The panels follow the daily units, so a short-running appliance adds only its few units. It still counts in the running load, which sets a hybrid inverter and its surge rating; an on-grid inverter follows the panels.
